prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1338; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a side impact at an intersection involving the insured vehicle and a second vehicle. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver of the insured vehicle is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of the loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact. Witness statements and scene photos are consistent with the account given at first notice.

Entry 4: Spoke with the other driver, who described the collision the same way the claimant did. Their account matches the sequence recorded by the responding officer.

Entry 5: Reviewed the vehicle file and found no prior damage to the vehicle on record. The repair estimate covers the visible side panels and door structure from this impact.

Entry 6: Claimant reports neck and upper back pain consistent with whiplash following the collision. The reported symptoms are a plausible result of a crash of this type.

Entry 7: Medical records show treatment followed a usual course, with symptoms easing steadily as the patient improved. No prior injury to the same body area appears in the records provided.

Entry 8: Called counsel to request the complete treatment history and billing. Counsel agreed to provide the records within the agreed timeframe.

Entry 9: Spoke with the claimant again, who gave the same account of the accident as in earlier conversations, with no changes to the sequence or the injuries described.

Entry 10: Reviewed the repair photos against the damage pattern. It is not yet clear whether all of the damage came from this impact, so the independent appraiser has been asked to check the lower body panels.

Entry 11: Appraiser review requested and medical records under review. Claim remains open pending the appraisal findings and final treatment billing.
